title: The Doorway
frame: The course’s last charge was “stay with the men you walked with.” This is where you say it to them.

slots.stem: To the men I walked with, I am
slots.prompt: Twelve weeks are done. Start with the men. One word for what you feel toward them now — the row has some — then why, in a few words.
slots.ex: To the men I walked with, I am hopeful and restless, wanting what the future offers, sometimes expecting that today.

slots.stem: What I saw in you was
slots.prompt: Name the gold. Not what they did for you — who they showed themselves to be. One thing, said plainly.
slots.ex: What I saw in you was men who told the truth before it was safe to.

title: Where I started
frame: Start where you started. Three lines, and a picture a man could see.

slots.stem: When I started, I was
slots.prompt: Go back to the first week. Where were you — the place, the time of day, what was going on at home? A picture, not a label.
slots.ex: When I started, I was sitting in the truck in the driveway, not ready to go in the house.

slots.stem: What I told myself was
slots.prompt: Now the sentence you were living on then — the one you said to yourself to get through the day. “I’ve got it handled.” “Nobody needs to know.” Short.
slots.ex: What I told myself was that I had it handled.

slots.stem: What nobody knew was
slots.prompt: And the part of it no one could see from outside.
slots.ex: What nobody knew was that this has been a lifetime of hiding.

title: What changed
frame: Time didn’t change you. The work you did in this room did. Say what is different, in three places: body, soul, spirit.

slots.stem: What came in through my eyes and ears was
slots.prompt: Week 1 called it your Sphere of Influence: “any sound, sight, smell, or touch, you control.” And: “The enemy has had free rein inside your SOI, and he’s been bringing his trash in with him.” What was coming in?
slots.ex: What came in through my eyes and ears was the sights and sounds of desire and satisfaction, something so absent from my real life.

slots.stem: What I take in now is
slots.prompt: The same eyes and ears. Now you are the gatekeeper for what comes in. What do you let in — a first thing in the morning, a habit that has held, a practice you took up? Pick from the row, or write your own.
slots.ex: What I take in now is the view of the room from my knees, the walk with prayer as my partner, the study times where I seek relationship.
slots.rowNote: From Richard Foster’s Celebration of Discipline. Walk With Me teaches all twelve.

slots.stem: What is being renewed in me is
slots.prompt: Pick where it is happening, then say what is new there.
slots.ex: What is being renewed in me is the way I engage the community, my family and friends; I lead with grace instead of contempt, and shame has nowhere to hide.
words: how I name what I feel
what I do first in the morning

slots.stem: Between me and God, what is growing is
slots.prompt: Spirit is where you and God meet. Of faith, hope and love, which one grew — and what does it look like in an ordinary week?
slots.ex: Between me and God, what is growing is desire to know Him more and faith in the path to do that.

title: Between the lines
frame: Two of your lines. What happened between them?

slots.prompt: A day, a place, something said or done. One or two sentences; the row has some ways to start.
slots.ex: What happened next was a week I almost skipped, and didn’t.

bridge.b: What I take in now is

title: What God did
scene: I will turn their mourning into joy; I will comfort them, and give them gladness for sorrow. — Jeremiah 31:13
frame: If it is still quiet and the struggle is still here, say that. It is not failure. This takes years, not weeks, and God’s answer may be as small as a room with men in it.

slots.stem: You saw me
slots.prompt: Not the story itself — the night you told it. What did the men do with it? In a room like that, shame has no place to hide.
slots.ex: You saw me, and I’m not sure which night or exactly what I said. What I remember is learning to trust as the nights became the source of community I had longed for.

slots.stem: What I expected was
slots.prompt: Before you said it out loud — what did you brace for? Being judged, being handled, the room going quiet.
slots.ex: What I expected was that no one would care, understand or accept me. I was afraid to be known.

slots.stem: What happened instead was
slots.prompt: What they did. Say it plainly; it is the part a man needs to hear.
slots.ex: What happened instead was a man said “me too.”

slots.stem: I asked him for
slots.prompt: What did you ask God for at the start? Say it the way you said it then. Not every ask is answered yet.
slots.ex: I asked him for death or life. Either way I was ready to surrender everything I had become.

slots.stem: What God did was
slots.prompt: Say what he did, not what you did. For some men it is this: a room with men in it, and what got named there. If nothing has moved yet, say that — it is true, and it belongs here.
slots.ex: What God did was set the path ahead with men that had already walked it, a freedom trail merchandised with the right mix of beautiful views, difficult terrain and resting spots.

title: Between the lines
frame: Two more pairs of your lines. What happened between each?

slots.prompt: The thing nobody knew, and the night the men saw you. What happened in between — a day, a place, something said or done?
slots.ex: It took weeks, but one night I said it out loud before I could talk myself out of it.

slots.prompt: What you asked him for, and what he did. How long did it take, and what did the waiting look like?
slots.ex: While that was going on, I kept asking, and for a month nothing changed except that I kept showing up.

title: What I take with me
scene: Jesus turned and saw them following and said to them, “What are you seeking?” — John 1:38
frame: His first question to the men who followed him. Answer it for a year from now.

slots.stem: My hope for the future is
slots.prompt: A year down the trail — what do you want to be true? Say it as a man who means to get there.
slots.ex: My hope for the future is to know God more intimately, grow in faith, offer my testimony in community.

slots.stem: What I will miss is
slots.prompt: An ending is a loss, even a good one. Say what aches. It is holy ground, not weakness.
slots.ex: What I will miss is knowing that once a week someone would ask.

slots.stem: What I ask of you is
slots.prompt: The twelve weeks are done. What do you need from these men now?
slots.ex: What I ask of you is to remember me, consider me, reach out to me when you do and expect of me the same.

slots.stem: Going forward, with this group, I will
slots.prompt: Yes or no — say it plainly and own it. Both are honorable. A goodbye said well is an ending done right.
slots.ex: Going forward, with this group, I will say thank you for walking this path with me and goodbye for now. I hope we can join one another on another path in the future.

slots.stem: The one small thing I will try this month is
slots.prompt: Not the whole life. One small thing, repeated, that moves you one degree — something you could start tomorrow.
slots.ex: The one small thing I will try this month is joining a circle of men that chose to grow with the community of believers.

slots.stem: I’ll know it has held when
slots.prompt: How will you know? Something you could see or count, four weeks from now.
slots.ex: I’ll know it has held when it is still happening four weeks from now.

slots.stem: I’ll know I’ve drifted when
slots.prompt: Name the sign before it comes — what you will be doing, and what you will be feeling. Pick from the rows, or write your own.
slots.ex: I’ll know I’ve drifted when my phone goes quiet and I tell myself I’m fine.

slots.stem: The voice that calls me back says
slots.prompt: Not a name — the words. What does it say?
slots.ex: The voice that calls me back says what it said the first time: surrender.

slots.stem: I will answer it by
slots.prompt: Week 12: “The days are not the achievement. Whatever you did that made the days is the achievement. Find it, name it out loud in the room, and do it again.” Pick one, or write your own.
slots.ex: I will answer it by reading my journal and reaching out for coffee.

title: Set a stone
scene: When your children ask in time to come, ‘What do those stones mean to you?’ then you shall tell them… So these stones shall be to the people of Israel a memorial forever. — Joshua 4:6–7
frame: Israel set twelve stones at the Jordan so that when their children asked “What do those stones mean to you?” there would be an answer. A stone is set to be found again — by you, and by whoever asks. Choose yours: one of your own lines above, or the words you walk by.

slots.prompt: Or your own words.
slots.ex: I asked him for death or life. Either way I was ready to surrender everything I had become.

slots.stem: This stone is for
slots.prompt: Naming well is a skill. Name the one this is for, and you will name other things well too.
slots.ex: This stone is for those who chose the same path.
words: someone who will ask one day
